output.generality: Helps correlated EXISTS and IN subqueries that join on equality, where the outer query is filtered and the subquery is only filters, projections and inner or semi joins: no aggregate, window, limit, order or nested subquery. Instead of a DISTINCT over the outer keys plus an extra join, it runs one semi join, which the join order optimizer can flip so the outer side is the build. Any RIGHT_SEMI or RIGHT_ANTI hash join, such as IN or EXISTS where the optimizer builds on the outer side, can now push min/max and Bloom filters into the probe scan. Unchanged: ANTI/MARK/SINGLE delim joins (NOT EXISTS keeps its current plan), subqueries with aggregates (q17/q02 style), non-equality correlations (q21-style `<>`), and delim joins with several DelimGets. Possible downside: if the plain semi join is not flipped and the big side stays the build side, the subquery scan loses the reduction that the delim inner join gave it.
output.notes: The biggest remaining gain on q04 is getting the Bloom filter through the compressed-materialization projection. Compressed materialization turns the join key into a UINTEGER with an offset, so the Bloom filter is skipped (`has_cast` / `storage_offset` check in physical_hash_join.cpp FinalizeFilters). The memory note on the exact Bloom filter through the offset describes a port: BFTableFilter key offset plus exact-bitmap mode built from the raw compressed min/max. It needs a header change and is a separate idea. It should cut the lineitem probe from 37.9M to about 2.3M rows. Also, without step (2) the deliminated plan had no join filters at all, because delim join conditions are `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`.
